interest: Tracks Japanese passports from prewar exchanges through wartime censorship to SCAP travel controls.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.0128, spanning August 1940 through December 1948) documents United States diplomatic, intelligence, and administrative oversight regarding Japanese passports and nationality documentation before, during, and after World War II. Prewar records (1940–1941) address the transmission of specimen copies of a revised Japanese multiple-trip passport by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo to Washington for use by the State Department and the Office of Naval Intelligence, as well as the routine return to the Japanese Embassy of a passport belonging to a deceased Japanese resident in Minneapolis. Wartime materials (1941–1944) comprise Office of Censorship intercepts of letters from Japanese community associations in California requesting passport verifications from prefectural governments in Japan, State Department inquiries into whether martial law in Hawaii hindered the Swedish protecting power from renewing Japanese passports, and cross-references regarding passports forwarded to the Spanish Embassy. Postwar records (1948) consist of circular instructions and standing operating procedures governing travel documentation for Japanese nationals and natives of Okinawa under Allied occupation, establishing that all passport issuance and extensions required explicit authorization from the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP).

subfiles.about: Circular instruction transmitting SCAP regulations and an Army memorandum governing travel documentation and passport extensions for Japanese nationals.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits Foreign Service Serial No. 951 and an enclosed Department of the Army Civil Affairs Division memorandum to American diplomatic and consular officers. The instruction outlines SCAP policies restricting Japanese passport issuance to authorized trade and cultural exchange travel, requiring destination countries to issue certificates of identity for permanent emigrants, and permitting nationality certificates in hardship cases. The enclosed standing operating procedure specifies how sponsors must apply to SCAP to extend passport validity for Japanese nationals abroad, and directs U.S. military attachés to endorse authorized extensions on page 6 of the passports.
subfiles.title: Foreign Service Serial No. 951: Travel Documentation of Japanese Nationals, with Army SOP Enclosure

subfiles.about: Central State Department file copy of Foreign Service Serial No. 951 and the attached Army standing operating procedure on passport extensions.
subfiles.summary: This is the central record file copy of Foreign Service Serial No. 951 (bearing file number 894.0128/12-2148), setting forth occupation regulations for Japanese travel documentation and passport extensions. It details SCAP requirements for Japanese nationals and notes that equivalent travel documentation for natives of Okinawa must be issued by U.S. Military Government authorities in the Ryukyus rather than the Japanese Government. The attached standing operating procedure governs sponsor guarantees and administrative endorsements by U.S. military attachés for extending Japanese passports abroad.
subfiles.title: Foreign Service Serial No. 951: Travel Documentation of Japanese Nationals (Record Copy with Enclosure)
